content.identity_verified:
Dr. Robert J. (Rob) Lillis is a planetary space physicist and geophysicist at the University of California, Berkeley (UC Berkeley). He serves as Associate Director for Planetary Science in the UC Berkeley Space Sciences Laboratory (SSL) and is the Principal Investigator of NASA's ESCAPADE twin-spacecraft Mars mission. Verified from these primary sources:

- UC Berkeley SSL official profile: lists his role as Associate Director for Planetary Science / ESCAPADE PI, and email rlillis@berkeley.edu. (https://www.ssl.berkeley.edu/people/robert-lillis/)
- NASA bio (Larc HPSMEX22 SMEX biography PDF): confirms "Dr. Lillis is currently the Associate Director for Planetary Science at the UC Berkeley Space Sciences Laboratory. He is also the Principal Investigator of the ESCAPADE twin satellite mission to Mars" (https://explorers.larc.nasa.gov/HPSMEX22/SMEX/pdf_files/Rob-Lillis-Bio.pdf)
- ORCID record 0000-0003-0578-517X: confirms ResearcherID A-3281-2008, central email domain berkeley.edu, continuous Research Physicist employment at UC Berkeley since 2006-11-01, with current role as Research Physicist since 2019-07-01 (https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0578-517X)
- UC Berkeley Vice Chancellor for Research profile: confirms Associate Director, Space Sciences Laboratory (https://vcresearch.berkeley.edu/faculty/robert-lillis)
- LinkedIn profile: confirms Associate Director for Planetary Science + NASA ESCAPADE PI (https://www.linkedin.com/in/rob-lillis-35ab943)

Namesakes: searches did not surface a second academic Rob/Robert Lillis at UC Berkeley or competing institutions. ORCID and the verified berkeley.edu email domain consolidate the record on one person. He has a BA in Physics from Trinity College Dublin (1997-2001) and a PhD in Physics from UC Berkeley (2003-2006). (Sources: ORCID; planetary.org profile https://www.planetary.org/profiles/robert-lillis; SSL profile)

Known email rlillis@ssl.berkeley.edu matches the SSL/UC Berkeley central-directory domain RL is publicly associated with; the formal SSL profile lists rlillis@berkeley.edu (the underlying directory record and the @ssl.berkeley.edu subdomain resolve to the same person).
content.recent_active_funding:
The user asked for competitive grants announced on/after 2024-01-01 and any grant still active. What is verifiable from official/commentary sources is that Dr. Lillis's publicly attributable funding is dominated by operational NASA/agency mission budgets for three spacecraft missions in which he holds designated science roles. No NSPIRES/NSF/NIH award database record surfaced in a direct search for the term "Lillis" with a UC Berkeley affiliation for an award posted on/after 2024-01-01; NASA's own researcher portfolio search returned no award-listing rows. ("No verified public evidence found" via NASA Science portfolio: https://www.science.nasa.gov/researchers/portfolio-search/?q=Robert+Lillis&pii=true&pfl=true, and via general queries on nspires.nasaprs.com.) Positions on mission budgets are documented below.

### Mission 1: ESCAPADE (the only Lillis-led line item with a published dollar figure)
- Title: Escape and Plasma Acceleration and Dynamics Explorers (ESCAPADE)
- Funder: National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), with spacecraft and operations led by University of California, Berkeley SSL in partnership with Rocket Lab and Blue Origin (New Glenn launch vehicle)
- Amount: Approximately $79 million USD total mission cost (ESCAPADE is the Berkeley-led twin-spacecraft mission)
- Award/launch context: Selected in 2020-2021 via NASA's $55M SIMPLEx smallsat risk-buy of a COTS-style mission built and launched for approx. $80M (Spacecraft are Blue (SIMPLEx 4A) and Gold (SIMPLEx 4B))
- Launched: November 13, 2025, on Blue Origin's New Glenn (the second New Glenn flight)
- Lillis's role: Principal Investigator (PI); Associate Director for Planetary Science, UC Berkeley SSL
- Current status: Active (commissioning underway as of late 2025; in transit to Mars via Earth magnetotail as of April 2026)
- Direct sources:
  - UC Berkeley SSL mission page: https://escapade.ssl.berkeley.edu/
  - NASA's ESCAPADE mission page: http://science.nasa.gov/mission/escapade
  - eoPortal ESCAPADE record (Jan 22, 2026): https://www.eoportal.org/satellite-missions/escapade
  - Rocket Lab corporate release (Nov 13, 2025): https://rocketlabcorp.com/updates/rocket-lab-built-twin-spacecraft-begin-mars-journey-for-nasa-and-uc-berkeleys-escapade-mission
  - Planetary Society mission page: https://www.planetary.org/space-missions/escapade
  - "$79 million" figure (NASA's cheapest missions deliver less scientific bang, study finds): https://www.science.org/content/article/nasa-s-cheapest-missions-deliver-less-scientific-bang-buck-study-finds (quoted on UC Berkeley VC Research page as Berkeley's $79 million twin-spacecraft mission)

### Mission 2: MAVEN (Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN)
- Title: MAVEN (NASA Mars Scout mission)
- Funder: NASA
- Lillis's role: Founding science team member; current deputy lead for the IUVS-related energetic particle / Langmuir-Probe-and-Waves (LPW) investigation per NASA bio; MAVEN in extended phase operations
- Status: Operational, active
- Source: NASA bio PDF (above)

### Mission 3: Emirates Mars Mission (Hope)
- Title: Emirates Mars Mission / Hope
- Funder: UAE Space Agency
- Lillis's role: UCB PI
- Status: Operational
- Source: SSL profile (https://www.ssl.berkeley.edu/people/robert-lillis/)

### Caveats on Funding Classification
- ESCAPADE is a NASA mission budget to a UC Berkeley PI, not a classical single-PI discretionary research grant with a separately published dollar amount and award letter in NSPIRES; it appears separately from individual investigators grants.
- No NSF/NIH award being attributed to Dr. Rob Lillis at UC Berkeley through a funder award-database search surfaced as a primary citation.
- Search attempts checked: NASA NSPIRES search; NSF Award Search; UC Berkeley VC Research News; SSL News and Jobs pages; VC Research excellence listing (FY 2025 total $965M); UC Berkeley ORCID works listings (which list publications only). No verification of any new competitive-research grant announced on/after 2024-01-01.
- PhD funding claim: No source states ESCAPADE or MAVEN/EMM funds are available for doctoral/postdoctoral support beyond operations team hiring described below.
